clues.title: Plate: green (old), white or yellow (new)
text: South Korea uses a variety of different licence plates.
- Pre-2006 plates are short and **green**. These will still show up in the street view coverage.
- Post-2006 plates are **white** for private vehicles, and **yellow** for commercial vehicles. These can be long and short.

images.caption: South Korean plates: green (old), white and yellow (new)

clues.summary: Plates from before 2006 are short and green and still show up in coverage. Newer ones are white for private cars and yellow for commercial vehicles, short or long.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3, black, white or silver
text: Almost all road coverage in South Korea is made with a **Generation 3** camera.
In most, but not all, of the coverage, the back of the Google car is visible. You can see three colours: **black, white** and **silver**. The car never has an antenna.

images.caption: Google car roof from above in three colours: black (top), white (middle) and silver (bottom)

clues.summary: Nearly all coverage is the older Gen 3 camera (blurrier, softer colours). The back of the car is usually visible and is black, white or silver. It never has an antenna.

clues.title: Coverage: lots of autumn and winter
text: A considerable amount of the coverage was made during **autumn and winter**.
Note that more pleasant-looking spring and summer coverage is also not uncommon.
clues.summary: A lot of coverage was taken in autumn and winter, though nicer spring and summer coverage is common too.

clues.title: Language: Hangul, letters with circles
text: The Korean writing system ([Hangul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangul)) is very unique and recognizable. One of its standout features is the presence of **circles** in many of its letters. This sets it apart from most other East Asian writing systems.
clues.summary: A very distinct script where many letters contain circles. That sets it apart from other East Asian writing systems.

clues.title: Pole: black-yellow diagonal stripes
text: Utility poles almost always have these pole markings near the bottom, consisting of **black and yellow diagonal stripes**.
These markings look similar to the ones found in Taiwan. There are however two main differences:
- In South Korea, the stripes do not reach all the way to the bottom, whereas in Taiwan they do.
- In South Korea, the stripes are more yellow. In Taiwan, they have more of an orange tint.
clues.summary: Utility poles almost always have black and yellow diagonal stripes near the bottom. They stop above the ground and look more yellow than Taiwan's.

differs.how: Stripes reach the ground and look more orange

clues.title: Pole: tapered spike on top
text: Most poles have a tapered “**spike**” on top.
clues.summary: Most poles end in a tapered spike.

clues.title: Driving side: right
text: South Korea drives on the **right**.

images.caption: Road with traffic on the right; the red sign shows two-way traffic

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the right.

clues.title: Road lines: yellow centre, white edges
text: Roads generally have **yellow middle lines** and white outer lines.
clues.summary: Yellow middle lines and white outer lines.

clues.title: Road: red block markings
text: You can sometimes see **red block markings** on the road.
clues.summary: You can sometimes see red block markings painted on the road.

clues.title: Sign: yellow triangle warnings
text: Triangular warning signs have a **yellow** **background**.
Note that circular prohibition signs, such as speed signs, have a white background. Yield signs also have a white background.
clues.summary: Triangular warning signs have a yellow background. Round prohibition signs like speed limits and yield signs have a white background.

clues.title: Sign: blue arrow-shaped street names on poles
text: Street signs will be blue, **arrow-shaped** and commonly **hanging** from a metal bar mounted to utility poles.
clues.summary: Blue, arrow-shaped street signs hanging from a metal bar attached to utility poles.

clues.title: Sign: white text on green direction signs
text: Direction signs in South Korea have white text on a green background.
clues.summary: Direction signs have white text on a green background.

clues.title: Road: yellow-and-white speed bumps
text: Speed bumps are often painted **yellow and white**.
clues.summary: Speed bumps are often painted yellow and white.

clues.title: Sign: five-sided blue pedestrian crossing
text: South Korean pedestrian crossing signs can be easily recognised from the distinct **pentagonal shape** combined with the blue background.
clues.summary: Pedestrian crossing signs are blue and shaped like a pentagon.

clues.title: Houses: blue house-shaped address plates
text: Korean buildings have very distinctive **house numbers**. They are blue and usually are shaped quite literally like a house. The full address of the building is written on them, in both Hangul and Latin script.
Some places have unique house numbers, which you can use to region-guess. More information about this can be found in the spotlight section.
clues.summary: Buildings have blue address plates shaped like little houses, with the full address in Hangul and Latin letters. Some areas have unique plates you can use to guess the region.

clues.title: Bollard: black-white wedge
text: You will sometimes see these black and white wedge-shaped bollards. They have a **round yellow reflector** on the front, and a grey one on the back.
clues.summary: A black and white wedge-shaped bollard with a round yellow reflector on the front and a grey one on the back.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains almost always visible
text: The South Korean landscape is predominantly **mountainous**. It is very rare to not see at least some hills or mountains in the distance. Even in the flat areas, you can almost always see elevation on the horizon.
clues.summary: Mostly mountainous. You nearly always see hills or mountains in the distance, and even flat areas show elevation on the horizon.

clues.title: Houses: red brick
text: **Red brick** is a very common building material in South Korea.
clues.summary: Red brick is a very common building material.

clues.title: Houses: traditional tiled roofs
text: Many buildings have **traditional tiled roofs** like these. These often have decorative elements on the corners, and tend to have sides that curve slightly upwards. Blue roofs are quite common.
clues.summary: Many buildings have traditional tiled roofs with decorated corners and edges that curve slightly upward. Blue roofs are quite common.

clues.title: Coverage: spotty, cities and big highways
text: South Korea has fairly limited and **very spotty coverage**. Other than large highways, most of the coverage is concentrated in and around major cities.
clues.summary: Coverage is limited and spotty. Apart from large highways, most of it is in and around major cities.

clues.title: Phone numbers: area codes rise going south
text: **Area codes** in South Korea increase to the south, from 02 in the north, to 064 on Jeju. It is also notable that Seoul has the only two-digit area code in the country.
clues.summary: Area codes grow towards the south, from 02 in the north to 064 on the southern island. The capital has the only two-digit code.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 2 camera in two big cities
text: **Generation 2** coverage is almost exclusively found in Seoul and Busan. It can also be found on a couple of highways outside the cities, however almost all of that coverage has been overwritten.
clues.summary: The older Gen 2 camera (lower quality) is almost only in Seoul and Busan, plus a few highways, though most of that has been replaced.

clues.title: Google car: small camera above brake light
text: A **small camera** can be seen mounted above the brake light on the Street View car on coverage northeast of Seoul and around Pohang.
clues.summary: A small camera sits above the car's brake light, in coverage northeast of Seoul and around Pohang.

clues.title: Landscape: volcanic island, dark soil
text: Jeju is a **volcanic island** with a lot of dark volcanic dirt, where you can also often see volcanoes in the distance.
clues.summary: A volcanic island with lots of dark volcanic soil, and volcanoes often visible in the distance.

clues.title: Walls: dark volcanic rock
text: Jeju also has a lot of **rock walls**, made of **dark** volcanic rocks.
clues.summary: The same island has many rock walls built of dark volcanic stone.

clues.title: Landscape: totally flat, yellow-green fields
text: The area around Gimje can be recognised by being one of the only **completely flat** areas of South Korea, combined with the open, **yellow-green fields** along almost every road in the area.
clues.summary: The area around Gimje is one of the only completely flat areas, with open yellow-green fields along almost every road.

clues.title: Houses: address plate with big white top
text: House numbers in the Hampyeong region can be recognised from the **large white section** at the top of the sign.
clues.summary: In the Hampyeong region, house number plates have a large white section at the top.
